issues.chapterText: Franklin saw the old man's gravestone in 1768.
issues.sourceText: There my grandfather died and lies buried. We saw his gravestone in 1758.

issues.chapterText: When they heard old people at Ecton describe Thomas's character, people who had known Thomas remarked that had the death fallen on the same day, "one might have supposed a transmigration."
issues.sourceText: The account we received of his life and character from some old people at Ecton, I remember, struck you as something extraordinary... "Had he died on the same day," you said, "one might have supposed a transmigration."
issues.fix: Attribute the remark to Franklin's son, who is addressed as "you," not to old people at Ecton.

issues.chapterText: around 1682 Josiah carried his wife and five children to New England
issues.sourceText: Josiah, my father, married young, and carried his wife with three children into New England, about 1682.
issues.fix: Change five children to three children.

issues.chapterText: In his first year he started at the head of his class and slipped to the middle.
issues.sourceText: I had risen gradually from the middle of the class of that year to be the head of it, and farther was removed into the next class above it
issues.fix: Reverse it: he rose from the middle of the class to the head of it, and was moved up a class.

issues.chapterText: because his early tutors had praised the boy's arithmetic, moved him to Mr. George Brownell's school for writing and arithmetic
issues.sourceText: altered his first intention, took me from the grammar-school, and sent me to a school for writing and arithmetic, kept by a then famous man, Mr. George Brownell
issues.fix: Delete the invented motive; the source gives only the cost of college and the mean livings as reasons.

issues.chapterText: Two generations later the pressure ran the other way
issues.fix: Drop the generation count; Josiah is three generations after the great-great-grandfather, and the source gives no such tally.

issues.chapterText: The registers went back only to 1455.
issues.sourceText: I found an account of their births, marriages and burials from the year 1555 only, there being no registers kept in that parish at any time preceding.

quizIssues.problem: The key points to "Timber left over from his father's candle and soap workshop," but the source and the question's own explanation both say a heap of stones intended for a new house near the marsh (choice 0). Set KEY to 0.
